title: Assets rail is headed 'categories'; every other surface calls them folders
body:
## Summary
The Assets tab's left rail is headed CATEGORIES, but the tree under it, the move dialog, the rename field and the tree's own landmark all call the same objects folders.

## Description
AssetsBrowser.tsx:52 renders 'categories' above <FolderTree>. FolderTree names its landmark 'Asset folders' (FolderTree.tsx:71), its rename field 'Rename folder ...' (:321), and draws Folder/FolderOpen glyphs (:275-279). MoveDialog, opened from a tile in the same rail, says 'folders on the shelf' (MoveDialog.tsx:321), 'No folders on the shelf yet' (:327), 'or a new folder inside it' (:359) and 'several folders'/'no folder' (:292). The data type is FolderNode (lib/assets). That's one concept with two names, and the odd one out is the visible heading. A screen-reader user hears 'Asset folders' navigation under a visible 'categories' heading.

## Flow
- Open Assets: heading CATEGORIES, rows drawn as folders
- Right-click a tile -> Move: 'FOLDERS ON THE SHELF'
- Fix: change the heading text to 'folders' (no other change)

## Expected impact
One name for the filing unit across the Assets tab, its dialog and its accessible landmark.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the filing unit has one name on the Assets tab
Before: rendered 'categor*' strings in app/library/*.tsx = 1 vs 'folder' >= 7
After: 'categor*' = 0
Method: probe - grep count
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/AssetsBrowser.tsx:52 'categories'; app/library/FolderTree.tsx:71 aria-label='Asset folders', :321 'Rename folder', :275-279 Folder glyphs; app/library/MoveDialog.tsx:292,321,327,359; grep -rn categor app/library/*.tsx -> 1 hit

title: Folder rails mark selection by colour only; MoveDialog uses aria-pressed
body:
## Summary
The Assets folder tree and the studio-embedded LibraryShelves rail are single-select filters whose current row is only tinted cyan. The sibling MoveDialog list, built from the same tree, announces its selection.

## Description
FolderTree.tsx:230-240 tints the row `bg-cyan-400/10 text-cyan-200` when `active`, and the selecting `<button>` at :261-282 carries no aria-current/aria-pressed. That covers the 'All assets' row (:75-81) too. LibraryShelves.tsx:192-196 RailRow (kind + collections, shown inside the studio) does the same. MoveDialog.tsx:333-336 lists the same FolderNode tree and sets `aria-pressed={active}`. A screen-reader user filtering the shelf can't tell which folder the gallery is showing. Inside FolderTree's `<nav>` the right attribute is `aria-current="true"` on the active folder button. RailRow toggles a filter, so `aria-pressed` fits there.

## Flow
- Select 'presets' in the Assets rail; the screen reader announces 'presets 30, button', the same as every other row
- Fix: FolderTree Row button: `aria-current={active ? "true" : undefined}`; LibraryShelves RailRow button: `type="button" aria-pressed={active}`

## Expected impact
The selected folder or filter is announced in both rails, matching MoveDialog.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the active folder/filter in each rail is exposed to assistive tech
Before: aria-current + aria-pressed in FolderTree.tsx = 0, LibraryShelves.tsx = 0 (MoveDialog.tsx = 1)
After: FolderTree.tsx >= 1, LibraryShelves.tsx >= 1
Method: probe - grep count
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/FolderTree.tsx:230-240 (colour-only active), :261-282 (button with no state attr), :75-81 (All assets row); app/_library/LibraryShelves.tsx:192-196 (RailRow colour-only); app/library/MoveDialog.tsx:333-336 (aria-pressed sibling); grep -c 'aria-pressed\|aria-current': FolderTree 0, LibraryShelves 0, MoveDialog 1

title: Two destructive buttons hand-roll <Button variant="danger"> class-for-class
body:
## Summary
'Delete the style' (proof-sheet delete confirm) and 'Remove from shelf' (plate viewer) re-type the exact rose classes that the Button primitive's `danger` variant already owns. In the confirm footer, the hand-rolled one sits next to a real `<Button variant="ghost">`.

## Description
Primitives.tsx:75-76 `danger` = `font-jetbrains border border-rose-400/40 bg-rose-400/10 text-rose-200 hover:bg-rose-400/20`. parts.tsx:302-307 (ConfirmDeleteStyle footer) and AssetLightbox.tsx:149-155 (viewer footer) spell those same five classes on a raw <button>. Because they bypass the primitive, they don't get (a) the primitive's explicit `focus-visible:outline-2 outline-offset-2`, (b) `disabled:opacity-50`, or (c) the world switch: under a WorldProvider 'almanac' the primitive renders `k-btn--danger` (Primitives.tsx:49-56), while these stay Obsidian rose beside a ghost button that has changed world. 'Keep it' at parts.tsx:299 is already the primitive, so the two buttons in one footer are built two different ways. The repo's rule (signal README) is that a second spelling of an existing chrome element isn't allowed.

## Flow
- Open 'delete this style' -> footer: <Button ghost> 'Keep it' + raw rose <button> 'Delete the style'
- Open a plate -> footer: raw rose 'Remove from shelf'
- Fix: replace both with `<Button variant="danger" className="cursor-pointer px-5 py-2">` / `px-4 py-1.5`, keeping onClick and label

## Expected impact
Destructive actions in the library go through the one primitive, so focus ring, disabled state and world theming stay consistent.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every destructive library button is the shared primitive
Before: raw-button sites carrying 'border-rose-400/40 bg-rose-400/10' in app/library/*.tsx = 2
After: 0 (both are <Button variant="danger">)
Method: probe - grep count
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/Primitives.tsx:43 (variant union incl. 'danger'), :49-56 (almanac branch), :75-76 (danger classes); app/library/parts.tsx:299 (<Button variant='ghost'> Keep it), :302-307 (raw rose button); app/library/AssetLightbox.tsx:149-155 (raw rose button); grep -n 'border border-rose-400/40 bg-rose-400/10' app/library/*.tsx -> 2 hits
verify: tests/golden-path/library-view-chrome.probe.spec.ts: in stripComments of parts.tsx and AssetLightbox.tsx, no `<button` opening tag contains `bg-rose-400/10` (2 on HEAD -> 0); both files contain `variant="danger"`. npm run typecheck; tests/golden-path/chrome-colour-literals.probe.spec.ts stays green.

title: Playground render failure isn't announced; the wall's read error is role=alert
body:
## Summary When a paid trial render fails or is refused, the error paragraph appears silently. The atelier's wall-read error two panes up is a role=alert region, so these sibling errors on one screen behave differently. ## Description Playground.tsx:351-355 renders `{error &&

{error}

}` with no live role. LibraryAtelier.tsx:394-397 renders the same rose treatment with `role="alert"`. A render takes seconds, and the user starts it and waits. For a screen-reader user the button goes from 'rendering...' back to 'render a trial' and nothing else is said, including the refusal-specific remedy at :233-235 ('Try a different subject — repeating this one will refuse again'), which is real error text and exempt from the narration law. Focus stays on the button, so nothing points the user at the message. ## Flow - Click 'render a trial' with a subject the vendor refuses - Sighted: rose box with the refusal; screen reader: silence - Fix: add `role="alert"` to the Playground error

(same as the wall alert) ## Expected impact Failed or refused renders, which may still cost money and need a different subject, are heard as well as seen. ## Evaluation Claim: user - a failed trial render is announced Before: role="alert" count in Playground.tsx = 0 (LibraryAtelier.tsx = 1) After: Playground.tsx = 1 Method: probe - grep count Result: better Gate: none
evidence:
app/library/Playground.tsx:230-238 (error set, incl. refusal remedy), :351-355 (error

, no role); app/library/LibraryAtelier.tsx:394-397 (role="alert" sibling); grep -c 'role="alert"' Playground.tsx = 0
verify:
tests/golden-path/library-view-chrome.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(app/library/Playground.tsx) contains `role="alert"` (0 on HEAD). Not the Notice.tsx role=status item; this is a raw

.

title: Price and trial prose hides in title={expr}: unreachable, unratcheted
body:
## Summary
Two native tooltips in the Playground are bound through expressions, so check:narration's literal `title="..."` regex never sees them. One is a 25-word, two-sentence explanation on a non-focusable span, which keyboard and touch users can't open.

## Description
Playground.tsx:300 `title={estimate.title}` sits on a plain <span> (not focusable). priceLabel (:111-126) supplies 'The price table could not be reached, so this render's cost is not known in advance. Whatever it actually costs is reported under the image afterwards.' (151 chars) and 'Asking /api/imaging/pricing what a render costs.' (48 chars, the app describing its own fetch). Both are over the gate's 45-char prose threshold (pipeline/check-narration.mjs:59), but the gate only matches `title="([^"]+)"` (:148), so these escape the 5/5 ratchet. Playground.tsx:261 `title={`${t.problem} · ${t.beat}`}` on the trial chips works the same way (e.g. 'quantity · HOOK · the record high, then half of it gone'). That is work content, but a native title doesn't show on keyboard focus. The signal README says native title is the wrong carrier and `<Hint>` is the right one.

## Flow
- Price fetch fails -> amber 'price unknown'; its reason exists only as a hover tooltip on a span
- Fix: for the 'unknown' state, render `<Hint variant="warn" tone="amber">pricing unreachable · cost shows after the render</Hint>` (<=12 words) beside the text and drop the span's title; for 'checking', drop the title entirely; for undeclared/known, put `price.note` (server-written, the work) in a <Hint> instead of title. Trial chips: drop title= and carry `problem · beat` in a sr-only span referenced by aria-describedby (the beat is also on the asset lightbox)

## Expected impact
The money line's caveats reach keyboard and touch users, and the prose stops escaping the narration ratchet through an expression.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - price caveats are reachable by keyboard, and no prose-length tooltip evades check:narration
Before: expression-bound title= in Playground.tsx = 2 (one on a non-focusable span carrying 151 chars); gate sees 0 of them
After: 0 expression-bound prose titles; price caveat in a <Hint> (focusable, <=12 words, counted by the gate)
Method: probe - source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/library/Playground.tsx:111-126 (priceLabel prose titles), :298-302 (<span title={estimate.title}>), :261 (title={`${t.problem} · ${t.beat}`}); pipeline/check-narration.mjs:59 TITLE_PROSE_CHARS=45, :148 literal-only regex /title="([^"]+)"/; `node pipeline/check-narration.mjs` -> 5/5 long title= (these 2 not counted)
verify: tests/golden-path/library-view-chrome.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(app/library/Playground.tsx) does not match /title=\{/ (2 on HEAD -> 0) and imports Hint from @/components/ui/signal. npm run check:narration stays green (Hint body <=12 words); npm run typecheck.
